intro.title: Test Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React application that uses the Context API to share data between components without passing props manually. You will learn how to create a context, provide its value from a parent component, and consume it in child components. The main technologies involved are React's createContext, Provider, and useContext hook. This will help you understand how to manage global state efficiently in a React app.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications, testing React components with Context is essential for building maintainable user interfaces that rely on shared state. For example, in e-commerce platforms, product filtering components need to access the same filter state across multiple UI sections like sidebars, product grids, and breadcrumbs. Similarly, dashboard applications use Context to manage user authentication state, allowing components like navigation menus, profile panels, and permission-based modals to consistently reflect login status. By testing these Context-dependent components, developers ensure that state changes propagate correctly, preventing bugs in complex, interactive features like multi-step forms or real-time data visualizations.
